latest_release.name: Ladybird alpha 🐞
latest_release.body:
Today we're releasing the very first alpha of Ladybird, a brand new web browser with its own engine, built from scratch.

Thank you. This release exists because of everyone who contributed code, filed bugs, wrote tests, helped with specs, and sponsored or donated to the project. Years of work by hundreds of people went into this, and we couldn't be more excited to finally put it in your hands.

**[Download Ladybird for macOS and Linux](https://ladybird.org/download/)**

## What makes Ladybird different

- **Our own engine.** Ladybird isn't a fork or a wrapper around Chromium, WebKit or Gecko. HTML, CSS, the DOM, layout, JavaScript and WebAssembly are all implemented from scratch.
- **Independent.** Ladybird is developed by a non-profit and funded by sponsors and donors.
- **Developed in the open.** Everything happens in public on GitHub, under a permissive license, guided by the web standards.
- **Built on the open web.** We implement the specifications, match other browsers where real websites rely on it, and improve the specs as we go.

## Under the hood

Ladybird is not a toy renderer. The engine passes a large and growing share of the web-platform-tests suite, and in many areas it stands next to the established browsers. Here's a look at how it's built:

- A multi-process architecture: documents from different sites run in separate, sandboxed renderer processes, and image decoding and network connections happen out of process, separately for each site.
- A from-scratch JavaScript engine (LibJS) with an interpreter and a JIT compiler, and a WebAssembly implementation (LibWasm).
- A garbage-collected object model, and a codebase that is steadily adopting Rust for memory safety.
- Standards-first development: spec text is followed step by step in the code, which keeps the implementation easy to audit, and when we find gaps or ambiguities in the specs, we report them upstream.
- WebDriver support for automation, and support for the Firefox DevTools protocol, so you can inspect pages with tooling you already know.

## What to expect from an alpha

Honesty first: this is an alpha.

- Some sites won't work, and the browser will occasionally crash. You can report a broken site from inside the browser, and you can review any report before sending it.
- There are no security promises yet. If you find a vulnerability, please tell us following [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/blob/master/SECURITY.md).
- The alpha is a rolling channel and updates itself regularly, so improvements will reach you quickly.

## Get involved

- **Try it out:** browse your favorite sites, test your own, and report what breaks from inside the browser. Every report helps us prioritize.
- **Support us:** consider supporting the project through [sponsorship or donations](https://ladybird.org/#sponsors).
- **Follow along:** the source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird), and the community hangs out on [Discord](https://discord.gg/nvfjVJ4Svh).

Whether you've followed along for years or are just discovering Ladybird today, welcome. Download it, take it for a spin, and tell us what you think. 🐞

detail.readme:
# Ladybird

[Ladybird](https://ladybird.org) is a truly independent web browser, using a novel engine based on web standards.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Ladybird is in a pre-alpha state, and only suitable for use by developers
>

## Features

We aim to build a complete, usable browser for the modern web.

Ladybird uses a [multi-process architecture](Documentation/ProcessArchitecture.md) with a main UI process,
WebContent renderer processes, and helper processes for tasks such as networking, image decoding, compositing and media.

Documents from different sites run in separate renderer processes, each sandboxed from the rest of the system.
Image decoding and network connections are done out of process, separately for each site, to be more robust against
malicious content.

At the moment, many core library support components are inherited from SerenityOS:

- LibWeb: Web rendering engine
- LibJS: JavaScript engine
- LibWasm: WebAssembly implementation
- LibCrypto/LibTLS: Cryptography primitives and Transport Layer Security
- LibHTTP: HTTP/1.1 client
- LibGfx: 2D Graphics Library, Image Decoding and Rendering
- LibUnicode: Unicode and locale support
- LibMedia: Audio and video playback
- LibCore: Event loop, OS abstraction layer
- LibIPC: Inter-process communication

## How do I build and run this?

See [build instructions](Documentation/BuildInstructionsLadybird.md) for information on how to build Ladybird.

Ladybird runs on Linux, macOS, Windows (with WSL2), and many other \*Nixes.

## How do I read the documentation?

Code-related documentation can be found in the [documentation](Documentation/) folder.

## Get in touch and participate!

Join [our Discord server](https://discord.gg/nvfjVJ4Svh) to participate in issue and development discussions.

Please read [Getting involved with Ladybird](Documentation/GettingStartedContributing.md) if you're new to Ladybird and want to help.

Before opening an issue, please see the [issue policy](CONTRIBUTING.md#issue-policy) and the [detailed issue-reporting guidelines](ISSUES.md).

The project participation guidelines can be found in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## License

Ladybird is licensed under a 2-clause BSD license.
